resources.string: Ad Skipper
Ad Skipper
Watches YouTube and its picture-in-picture window for a visible "Skip Ad" control and activates it when it appears. Reads screen content from YouTube only.
Service is ON. Skippable YouTube ads will be skipped automatically.
Service is OFF. Turn it on to start skipping ads.
Service was stopped by the system. Accessibility settings will still show Ad Skipper as ON — turn it off and back on again to restart it.
Android does not let an app switch on its own accessibility service, so this last step is manual:\n\nSettings > Accessibility > Installed apps > Ad Skipper > On
Could not open Accessibility settings on this device. Open Settings and look for Accessibility > Installed apps > Ad Skipper.

Service running
A silent, ongoing notification shown while the skip service is active. It exists so device memory cleaners are less likely to stop Ad Skipper.
Ad Skipper is active
Watching YouTube for skippable ads.

Keeping it running on Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO:

1. Open Recents, pull down on the Ad Skipper card, and tap the padlock. Locked apps survive one-key clean and swipe-up clear — this is the important one.
2. Security app > Permissions > Autostart > enable Ad Skipper.
3. App info > Battery saver > No restrictions.

Keeping it running on Samsung:

1. Settings > Battery > Background usage limits > Never sleeping apps > add Ad Skipper.
2. App info > Battery > Unrestricted.
3. Make sure Ad Skipper is not listed under Deep sleeping apps.

Keeping it running on OnePlus/OPPO/realme:

1. App info > Battery usage > Allow background activity, and set battery optimisation to Don't optimise.
2. Recents > long-press the Ad Skipper card > Lock.
3. Settings > Battery > turn off Sleep standby optimisation if present.

Keeping it running on Huawei/Honor:

1. Settings > Battery > App launch > Ad Skipper > Manage manually, and enable all three switches.
2. Recents > swipe down on the Ad Skipper card to lock it.

Keeping it running on vivo/iQOO:

1. Settings > Battery > High background power consumption > allow Ad Skipper.
2. Settings > Apps > Autostart > enable Ad Skipper.
3. Recents > lock the Ad Skipper card.

Keeping it running:

If ads stop being skipped, your device is stopping the service in the background. Open App info below and remove any battery restriction on Ad Skipper, then lock it in Recents if your device offers that.

Stock Android re-starts the service by itself, so this mostly affects vendor ROMs. dontkillmyapp.com lists the exact steps per brand.
